title: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd - 544457 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q2 FY27 total income rose 10% to INR142 crore and PAT doubled to INR22 crore, driven by a 11% ADR increase.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 growth was rate-led, with portfolio ADR up 11% to about INR7,900 and occupancy flat at 75%, giving RevPAR up 10%. Consolidated EBITDA rose to INR52 crore from INR41 crore, with margin up to 36.7% despite a 1.4% GST 2.0 impact. Finance costs fell 28% to INR9.7 crore after IPO-funded debt repayment, lifting PAT to INR22 crore. F&B returned to 10% growth after a weak Q1 hit by West Asia-related cancellations. Management kept its mid-teens FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guidance and reduced the FY27 capex expectation slightly.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR41 crore in Q2 FY26; margin from 32%

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: ARR up 8% to INR9,400 and occupancy up to 81% from 78%, taking RevPAR up 12% to INR7,600; both rate and occupancy grew on corporate and MICE recovery.

segments.name: Other markets
segments.commentary: ARR up 13% to INR6,300 while occupancy fell to 70% from 74%, giving RevPAR up 8%; deliberate rate push in GIFT City and Mysore.

segments.name: Mysore (Grand Mercure / ibis Styles)
segments.commentary: Grand Mercure Mysore ARR up 27% YoY; ibis Styles Mysuru at 68% occupancy in its second full year.

segments.name: GIFT City (Grand Mercure Ahmedabad)
segments.commentary: ARR up 16% and RevPAR up 37% YoY.

segments.name: Courtyard Kochi Infopark (rebranded from Four Points)
segments.commentary: ARR up 17% in first full quarter post rebrand; occupancy declined and is expected to recover over 2-3 quarters. Management cited the hotel's occupancy at 40% in H1 and 66% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guidance of mid-teens maintained; management said it did not want to change guidance at this point.
H2 FY27 RevPAR expected to grow in the mid-teens range, with October trends and forward inquiries described as strong.
Target to lift each hotel's ADR above INR7,500 over the next few quarters.
Net debt to EBITDA expected at slightly below 4x in FY28-FY29 (said to be 3.5x to 4x); DSCR to stay around 2x to 2.5x.
FY27 capex now expected at around INR400 crore (earlier INR450 crore); FY28 capex allocation INR700 crore.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai (45 keys) expected to open in H2 FY27, likely end of Q3 or early Q4.
Two Fairfield by Marriott hotels (BIAL and Brigade Valencia, Bangalore) expected to open towards end of FY28.
Acquisition from unidentified IPO proceeds targeted as top priority in the next two to three quarters, with possible slippage by one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: Total planned expansion capex about INR3,600 crore; INR484 crore spent to 30 Sep 2026, of which INR84 crore in H1 FY27.
Further INR400-450 crore expected in H2 FY27, including capital earmarked for the unidentified acquisition.
Portfolio to expand from current base to 3,300 keys by FY31 with 1,700 keys under development; luxury and upper upscale mix to rise from 14% to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31.
Brands in pipeline include Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton across Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi and Bangalore.

Two hotels in Brigade Enterprises SPVs (Hyatt Regency ~350 keys; ~250-key hotel in Ananthay Properties) to be developed by SPVs and may move to BHVL later; construction targeted to start in two to three quarters.
Renewable energy accounts for 67% of total energy needs across the portfolio.
demand_pricing: Portfolio ADR up 11% YoY to about INR7,900 in Q2; domestic demand was 76% of customers, up 1% YoY.
F&B returned to 10% growth in Q2 after Q1 was hit by West Asia-related cancellations; management estimated a Q1 impact of about INR14 crore, or nearly 10% of top line.
Electronica conference in Bangalore (September) boosted both rooms and F&B; Space Expo also cited.
Q3 outlook: festive demand, wedding season with more good dates than last year, and large city-wide conferences already sold out hotel space.
October described as good, with the main business expected from the second week of November after Diwali holidays.
Hotel acquisition market is competitive: management said good-value assets are hard to find while the hotel industry is performing well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy diverge between Bangalore and other cities, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore assets are mature and stable. Mysore ibis Styles (2 years old) is being price-positioned and should reach stabilised occupancy next year; Kochi rebrand gave a 17% rate increase and displaced low-paying accounts, with stabilisation over 2-3 quarters. Management expects occupancy in other markets to reach Bangalore-like levels within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Brigade Enterprises hotel announcements (Bangalore SPVs) relevant to BHVL, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The two hotels (a Hyatt Regency in a 25-acre KIADB-land development and a 250-key hotel in the Ananthay township) sit in Brigade Enterprises SPVs and are not directly buyable now; they may move into BHVL later once future cash flows allow. Construction is expected to start within two to three quarters, pending design and approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of the rise in other non-current financial assets to about INR61 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly fixed deposits: surplus cash parked in long-term deposits, not electricity or utility deposits. The CFO confirmed the total of about INR177 crore plus INR62 crore cited as FDs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 RevPAR outlook and the capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 RevPAR grew 9% and Q2 about 10%; H2 is expected in the mid-teens range. FY27 capex now around INR400 crore versus INR450 crore earlier, with FY28 at INR700 crore and the larger ramp in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the peak net debt to EBITDA and the debt service coverage levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to EBITDA expected to be slightly below 4x in FY28-FY29, with a 3.5x to 4x range confirmed; DSCR should remain about 2x to 2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mid-teens guidance be beaten given the wedding calendar and conference bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose to keep the mid-teens range and said any upside would be a positive surprise, noting it needs to recover the roughly 10% top-line hit from Q1.

risks_watch: Occupancy gap in non-Bangalore hotels: Courtyard Kochi (ex-Four Points) and ibis Styles Mysuru need to lift occupancy; Sheraton Grand rate growth was marginal.
Execution risk on the INR400-450 crore H2 capex and on the unidentified acquisition, which may slip one to two quarters.
Capex slippage: FY27 spend running well below allocation (INR84 crore in H1 vs about INR450 crore plan).
Leverage peaking at 3.5x to 4x net debt to EBITDA in FY28-FY29 as the pipeline is funded.
F&B and MICE dependence on event calendar, given the Q1 cancellations linked to the West Asia crisis.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q2 rate-led growth and margin expansion, and on the H2 outlook. Cautious and somewhat evasive on specifics: no numerical RevPAR range or upgrade to guidance, and the acquisition timing was left open.
key_quotes: This quarter we did about 10% and for half year, it was 9%, but we expect the second half of the year to be better.
Our growth for this quarter is rate-led.
So, we believe that from the second week of November onwards is when we will really see a very vibrant business, I guess, in all the hotels.
I don't want to change the guidance at this point in time, but I am happy about the EBITDA increase for Q2, which is very encouraging.

adds.what: Two Fairfield by Marriott hotels (BIAL and Brigade Valencia, Bangalore)
Two SPV hotels (Hyatt Regency ~350 keys; ~250-key Ananthay Properties hotel), may move to BHVL later

growth.why: Mid-teens FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guidance was held, with H2 RevPAR guided up mid-teens on strong October trends and festive/conference bookings; Chennai 45-key Courtyard opens end Q3/early Q4 and FY27 capex trimmed to ~INR400 crore, but the Fairfield and SPV hotels are only 4+ quarters out, so delivery is only partly backed by specifics.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 36.7% from 32% and H1 margin reached 35.8% on rate-led growth (ADR +11%), with GST 2.0 drag easing to 1.6% in H1, though Q2 impact was 1.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Courtyard Chennai (45 keys) is guided to open end Q3 or early Q4 FY27, but the Fairfield hotels and SPV hotels are only expected towards end FY28 or later, so the near-term addition is small.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 RevPAR up mid-teens versus Q2 at about 10% and H1 at 9%, supported by festive, wedding and conference bookings, with occupancy flat at 75.2%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75.2%, below the 80% threshold, but the INR3,600 crore expansion plan with 1,700 keys under development and an unidentified acquisition as top priority makes further capex or deal announcements likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held mid-teens FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance and declined to raise it, with H1 total income only +7% and Q1 hit by about INR14 crore of West Asia cancellations still to recover.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex is running well below plan (INR84 crore in H1 vs about INR450 crore FY27 plan), the acquisition may slip one to two quarters, and Kochi and Mysuru occupancy is weak at 66% and 68%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai (45 keys) is expected to open end Q3 or early Q4, and the luxury mix is planned to rise from 14% to 31% by FY29, with Grand Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton in the pipeline.

rows.label: Unidentified IPO-funded acquisition
rows.why: Targeted as top priority in the next two to three quarters, with slippage of one to two quarters possible, and about INR400-450 crore of H2 FY27 capex includes earmarked capital for it.

rows.label: Courtyard Kochi occupancy recovery
rows.why: Occupancy fell to 66% in Q2 and 40% in H1 after the rebrand, with management guiding stabilisation over 2-3 quarters and a 17% ARR gain already achieved.

rows.label: Leverage peaks at 3.5-4x net debt/EBITDA
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA is guided at 3.5x to 4x in FY28-FY29 as the INR700 crore FY28 capex is funded, with DSCR around 2x to 2.5x and net cash of INR29 crore today.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 rate-led growth, margin expansion and H2 RevPAR up mid-teens, but cautious on specifics, holding guidance without an upgrade and leaving acquisition timing open; analysts pushed on occupancy gaps in non-Bangalore hotels, leverage peaks and capex slippage.
